Here's a production-ready ruleset I'd build for a fresh IIS box:

**1. HTTPS Redirect (highest priority)**
```
Name: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
Pattern: (.*)
Match URL / Absolute URL
Conditions: {HTTPS} != on
Action: Redirect, https://{HTTP_HOST}{REQUEST_URI}, permanent (301)
```
Why first: Avoids processing any subsequent rules on insecure connections.

**2. Canonical Host**
```
Name: Enforce Canonical Domain
Pattern: (.*)
Conditions: {HTTP_HOST} != www.example.com
Action: Redirect, https://www.example.com/{R:1}, permanent (301)
```
Why: Consolidates domain variants (example.com → www.example.com, or vice versa per your preference). Prevents duplicate content issues and simplifies CDN/caching.

**3. Trailing Slash Normalization**
```
Name: Remove Trailing Slash (directories)
Pattern: (.*?)/$
Conditions: {REQUEST_FILENAME} is a directory = false, {REQUEST_FILENAME} is a file = false
Action: Redirect, https://{HTTP_HOST}/{R:1}, permanent (301)
```
Why: Prevents /page/ and /page from being indexed as separate resources.

**4. Static Content Passthrough**
```
Name: Skip Rewrite for Static Assets
Pattern: .*
Conditions: {REQUEST_FILENAME} matches pattern \.(jpg|jpeg|png|gif|css|js|ico|woff|woff2)$
Action: None
```
Why: Stops rewriting static files—better performance, cleaner logs.

**5. Application Routing (if applicable)**
```
Name: Route to Application
Pattern: ^(.*)$
Conditions: {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a file, {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a directory
Action: Rewrite, /index.aspx?path={R:1}
```
Why: Handles clean URL schemes for dynamic apps without exposing file structure.

**Order matters:** HTTPS → canonical domain → normalization → static skip → app logic. This prevents redirects from compounding and ensures security rules fire before rewrites.

Here's a production-ready IIS URL Rewrite ruleset I'd build from scratch:

**Rule 1: Force HTTPS**
```
Condition: {HTTPS} is not "on"
Action: Redirect to https://{HTTP_HOST}{REQUEST_URI} (301)
Exception: /.well-known/* (for ACME cert validation)
```
Why: HTTPS-first eliminates protocol downgrade attacks and is non-negotiable for any production site now.

**Rule 2: Enforce Canonical Host**
```
Condition: {HTTP_HOST} matches ^www\. or matches your-domain.local|staging variants
Action: Redirect to https://canonical.example.com{REQUEST_URI} (301)
```
Why: Prevents duplicate content penalties, consolidates session/cookie handling, and gives you one authoritative hostname.

**Rule 3: Remove Trailing Slashes (conditional)**
```
Condition: {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a directory AND {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a file AND request ends with /
Action: Redirect to {REQUEST_URI} minus trailing slash (301)
Exception: Root / stays as-is
```
Why: Avoids dual-content issues. Adjust this based on your CMS — some frameworks need trailing slashes.

**Rule 4: Route Requests to Application**
```
Condition: {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a file AND {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a directory
Action: Rewrite to index.aspx or your entry point
```
Why: Lets your framework handle routing without exposing internal structure.

**Ordering matters**: HTTPS first, then host canonicalization, then app routing. IIS stops at the first rewrite unless you set `stopProcessing="false"`.

**Additional production considerations:**
- Enable compression on responses
- Test rule order with real traffic patterns (mixed protocols, subdomains)
- Use rewrite maps for complex domain redirects if you have many

Here's a production-ready ruleset I'd build in order of execution:

**1. HTTP to HTTPS Redirect (Catch-All)**
```
Pattern: (.*)
Condition: {HTTPS} != "on"
Action: Redirect to https://{HTTP_HOST}/{R:1} (301)
```
Why first: Enforce encryption before any other logic. Non-negotiable for modern deployments.

**2. Canonical Host Redirect**
```
Pattern: (.*)
Condition: {HTTP_HOST} != "www.example.com"
Action: Redirect to https://www.example.com/{R:1} (301)
```
Why: Consolidate www/non-www variants. Pick one canonical form (www or bare domain based on your DNS setup). This prevents duplicate content and consolidates authority signals.

**3. Trailing Slash Normalization (Optional)**
```
Pattern: ^(.*[^/])$
Condition: {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a directory AND {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a file
Action: Redirect to {R:1}/ (301)
```
Why: Consistency. Decide if you want trailing slashes; be consistent. Reduces 404s from user typing variations.

**4. Static File Pass-Through**
```
Pattern: ^(.*\.(jpg|png|css|js|ico|woff|woff2))$
Condition: {REQUEST_FILENAME} matches pattern [keep this separate]
Action: None (pass through - no rewrite)
```
Why: Don't waste cycles rewriting assets. Short-circuit static content to file system.

**5. Application Routing (if applicable)**
```
Pattern: ^(.*)$
Condition: {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a file AND {REQUEST_FILENAME} is not a directory
Action: Rewrite to index.php?path={R:1} (or your app entry point)
```
Why: Routes unknown paths to your application router instead of 404.

**Execution order matters:** Place redirects (1-3) before rewrites (4-5). Redirects change the request; rewrites reprocess it internally.

**Key practices:**
- Use 301 (permanent) for canonical/structural changes; 302 for temporary
- Keep conditions specific to avoid performance drag
- Test with common patterns: `/`, `/page`, `/page/`, `/static/image.jpg`
- Monitor redirect chains in browser dev tools
